title: Observability pipeline debugging notes (tracing/metrics/logs) - Eli WIP 2
body:
TL;DR: Intermittent drop in traces and metrics started 2026-03-02 13:45 UTC. Logs are backfilling slowly; some services missing correlation headers (traceparent/trace_id). Hypothesis: combination of otel-collector canary + fluent-bit header-normalization change. Immediate mitigation: increase collector debug logging, enable raw span passthrough, and run trace-proxy harness.

Timeline / symptoms:
- 2026-03-02 13:40 UTC: Pager: >50% drop in traces ingested into traces-index (traces-per-second).
- 2026-03-02 13:45 UTC: request_latency metric present but p90/p99 telemetry missing for routes /generate and /chat/stream.
- 2026-03-02 13:47 UTC: Kibana: log ingestion lag; kafka consumer lag for topic observability-spans increased.
- 2026-03-02 14:00 UTC: Correlation IDs missing on some ingested logs (trace_id empty).

Recent changes (possible causes):
- otel-collector rolled to v0.83.0 (canary) 2026-02-28 in cluster-prod-a (deploy obs-collector-canary-20260228).
- logging-agent (fluent-bit fork) updated 2026-03-01 with header-normalization patch (PR #211).
- kafka brokers minor upgrade 2026-02-20 (unlikely).

Commands tried / quick checks (outputs trimmed):
1) Collector pods / logs:
$ kubectl get pods -n observability -l app=otel-collector
otel-collector-canary-abc123 1/1 Running 0 3d

$ kubectl logs otel-collector-canary-abc123 -n observability | tail -n 200
2026-03-03T00:12:01Z warn service/service.go: failed to process batch: error="failed to decode span: invalid trace id"
2026-03-03T00:12:02Z info receiver/otlpreceiver: accepted 312 spans
2026-03-03T00:12:02Z error exporter/kafka: write failed: EOF

Notes: repeated "invalid trace id" and occasional EOF writing to kafka. Could be malformed spans or header stripping upstream.

2) Kafka consumer group / lag:
$ kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-prod:9092 --describe --group obs-ingesters
TOPIC PARTITION CURRENT-OFFSET LOG-END-OFFSET LAG CONSUMER-ID
observability-spans 0 1234567 1239876 5310 consumer-7

Lag non-trivial; backfilling. Consumer logs show retries and "malformed record" exceptions.

3) Curl test with traceparent header to API gateway:
$ curl -v -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" https://api.redwood.dev/healthcheck
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-request-id: req_abc123
< x-trace-id:  (empty)  <-- header not propagated on some paths

4) Grep instrumentation logs for malformed spans:
/var/log/containers/service-a-xyz.log:2026-03-02T13:44:31Z ERROR invalid trace id: 00000000000000000000000000000000
/var/log/containers/service-b-xyz.log:2026-03-02T13:44:33Z WARN failed to read traceparent header: header missing

5) OTel collector config snippets:
- receivers: otlp
- processors: batch, memory_limiter
- exporters: kafka, jaeger
- extensions: health_check

Potential misconfig: kafka exporter tls settings changed with new sarama defaults may cause EOF. A new processor "resource/attributes/default" added in canary maps attributes and might accidentally overwrite traceid if misconfigured (VERIFY).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Fluent-bit header-normalization or upstream sidecar is stripping/normalizing traceparent and producing zero trace_id -> collector logs "invalid trace id". (probable)
2) otel-collector canary processor/exporter config mangles trace IDs or drops spans on unexpected attributes. (possible)
3) Kafka exporter intermittent EOF causing backpressure and pipeline stalls. (possible)
4) Consumer decoder/schema mismatch causing "malformed record" on consumer. (less likely)

Runbook steps taken / attempts:
- Repro locally: minimal service with OTLP to canary collector; observed "invalid trace id" when sending hyphenated/uppercase trace IDs -> suggests parser differences.
- Disabled header-normalization on one fluent-bit node (staging); traceparent preserved -> points to logging agent change.
- Scaled obs-ingesters by +2 (kubectl scale deployment/obs-ingesters --replicas=5) to reduce backlog; lag reduced but malformed record persists.
- Rolled sarama client to older version in producer canary to test EOF frequency; EOF still occasional.

Evidence to collect / instrumentation to add:
- Enable debug logging in logging-agent to capture raw incoming HTTP headers for sample requests (redact PII).
- Deploy small OTLP capture endpoint in front of collector to dump raw spans for offline analysis.
- Correlate ingress nginx logs, logging-agent, and collector timestamps to identify where trace_id disappears.
- Add metric in collector counting rejected spans with reason labels (invalid_trace_id, decode_error, exporter_error).

Short reproducible tests (commands):
1) Send 1000 requests with well-formed traceparent from canary client:
$ for i in $(seq 1 1000); do curl -s -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" https://canary.api.test/generate > /dev/null; done
Watch otel-collector logs for "invalid trace id" count.

2) Run OTLP posting script constructing spans with variants of traceid formatting (lowercase/uppercase/dashes) to find parser rejections.

3) Revert fluent-bit header normalization PR on one node pool and run load to compare.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Any instrumentation SDK updates between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-02? Check deploys.
- Network issues between collector and kafka causing EOF or producer misbehavior?
- Does the new collector processor mapping include a mapping for trace_id/traceparent by mistake? Need commit history review.

Temporary mitigations suggested:
- Roll back fluent-bit header normalization in prod canary until root cause identified.
- Increase otel-collector replicas temporarily to reduce tail-drop under exporter errors.
- Enable enhanced debug logs on collector and logging-agent for 6 hours and upload to s3 for analysis.

Breadcrumbs (commands to rerun):
- kubectl logs -n observability otel-collector-canary-abc123 | grep -i "invalid trace id" -n
- kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-prod:9092 --describe --group obs-ingesters
- kubectl exec -n observability -it otel-collector-canary-abc123 -- /bin/sh -c 'cat /etc/otel/config.yaml'
- grep -R "header-normaliz" /etc/fluent-bit/conf.d/ -n || true

TODO (short):
- [ ] Get config diffs for otel-collector between prod stable and canary (ACTION: Dom)
- [ ] Reproduce minimal malformed span locally and attach sample pcap/logs (ACTION: Amelia)
- [ ] Revert fluent-bit PR in prod canary (ACTION: Eli/Dom)
- [ ] Add per-reason rejected-spans metric to collector (ACTION: eng-observability)

Longer term ideas:
- Add end-to-end synthetic checks asserting trace->log->metrics correlation every minute (pipeline test).
- Enforce stricter contract in instrumentation SDKs to always emit valid trace_id and fail CI on invalid formatting.

Footer: saving iterative notes here. Will update after canary revert and debug captures.

-- Eli
